Request: Question from the CFO: 'In how many months this contract year did Acme miss its uptime SLA, and how much service credit are we owed?'

Your step: Locate the Acme contract and SLA policy documents, read the uptime SLA terms and credit schedule, review monthly performance/uptime reports for the current contract year, and use the 'SLA credit calculator' tool to determine exactly how many months Acme fell below the SLA threshold and the total service credit owed (convert any foreign currency amounts to the reporting currency using 'Currency converter (live)' if needed).

Facts gathered so

trace.why: The executor synthesizes the retrieved facts into the final answer for the CFO.
trace.detail:
MESSAGE:
Re: Acme Uptime SLA Performance – Contract Year Nov 2025 to Oct 2026 (Reviewed Through September 2026)

Per Clause 4.1 of the contract, Acme is required to maintain 99.9% monthly uptime. Reviewing monthly performance data from November 2025 through September 2026, Acme fell below this threshold in two months:

- May 2026: 99.42% uptime
- July 2026: 99.61% uptime

All other months in the period (November, December, January, February, March, April, June, August, and September) met or exceeded the 99.9% SLA target.

Under Clause 4.2, the service credit rate is 5% of the monthly fee (Rs 2,00,000) for each month uptime falls below SLA, i.e., Rs 10,000 per missed month. With two months of non-compliance (May and July 2026), the total service credit owed is:

2 months x Rs 10,000 = Rs 20,000

We will apply this credit against the next invoice cycle and request Acme's confirmation of the amount. Please let us know if you would like this credit invoiced separately or adjusted against the upcoming payment.

Nimbus Retail Procurement

INTERNAL NOTE:
Figures per Clause 4.1 (SLA target), Clause 4.2 (credit rate), and sla_credit_calculator output. Two SLA misses confirmed: May (99.42%) and July (99.61%). Credit = Rs 10,000/month x 2 = Rs 20,000. No unverified exchange rates used. Awaiting approval before sending to Acme.
